issue_snapshot.title: open_sftp() can block up to an hour
issue_snapshot.body:
Hey all, I want to report a bug that @VakarisZ and me found.

It comes from `open_sftp` function on SSHClient which can block up to an hour, if a machine is killed after connecting

To reproduce it just connect to a VM machine, set breakpoint before calling `open_sftp`, pause the VM machine and run the `open_sftp`. It will wait up to an hour until it timeouts. I have waited 14 minutes and then unpaused the VM which unblocked the `open_sftp` function.

What I purpose for a solution is that we add timeout argument to `open_sftp`.

Here is a snippet code I used to reproduce the block:

```import paramiko
import datetime
import pdb

ssh = paramiko.SSHClient()
ssh.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.WarningPolicy)

ssh.connect("x.x.x.x", port=22, username=username, password=password, timeout=10,
            auth_timeout=10, banner_timeout=5)

print(datetime.datetime.now())

pdb.set_trace()

with ssh.open_sftp() as ftp:
    print(datetime.datetime.now())


print(datetime.datetime.now())
```

issue_snapshot.title: Block-edit UI cannot persist explicit null for an Optional[str] field with a non-null default
issue_snapshot.body:
### First check

- [x] I added a descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar issue and didn't find it.
- [x] I searched the Prefect documentation for this issue.
- [x] I checked that this issue is related to Prefect and not one of its dependencies.

### Bug summary

Clearing an optional (`Optional[str]`) block field to empty in the block-edit UI and saving does **not** persist an explicit `null` for that field — it silently reverts the field to its Pydantic class default instead, with no error or warning. For a field whose non-null default has real behavioral meaning (not just a placeholder), this can silently change runtime behavior after what looks like a no-op edit.

### Root cause (traced in `ui-v2` source)

1. `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-string.tsx`:
   ```ts
   function handleChange(value: string | undefined) {
     onValueChange(value || undefined);
   }
   ```
   Clearing the textarea yields `value = ""`. Since `||` treats `""` as falsy, `"" || undefined` evaluates to `undefined` — **never** `null`. There is no code path in this widget that can report `null`.

2. `ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-object.tsx`, in the debounced flush that merges child property changes into the object's values:
   ```ts
   for (const { key, value } of patches.current) {
     newValues[key] = value;
     if (value === undefined) {
       delete newValues[key];
     }
   }
   ```
   Any property reported as `undefined` has its **key deleted** from the values object entirely, rather than being set to `null`.

3. `ui-v2/src/components/blocks/block-document-edit-page/block-document-edit-page.tsx`, on submit:
   ```ts
   updateBlockDocument(
     { id: blockDocument.id, data: values, merge_existing_data: false },
     ...
   )
   ```
   `merge_existing_data: false` performs a full replace of the block document's data with whatever `values` currently contains — now missing the key.

4. Server-side, a full-document Pydantic validation on save fills in the field's declared class default for any key absent from the submitted data — there is no validator/mechanism that can tell "explicitly cleared" apart from "never set."

Net effect: **it is currently impossible to persist an explicit `null` for an `Optional[str]` block field with a non-`None` default through the block-edit UI.** The only way to do it is via the Python SDK (`SomeBlock(some_field=None).save(..., overwrite=True)`), which sends the key with an explicit `null` and bypasses the UI's string-widget serialization entirely.

### Reproduction

1. Define a block with an `Optional[str]` field with a non-`None` default, e.g.:
   ```python
   from prefect.blocks.core import Block
   from typing import Optional

   class MyBlock(Block):
       format_rule: Optional[str] = "value.split(',')"
   ```
2. Save an instance with `format_rule=None` via Python: `MyBlock(format_rule=None).save("my-block")`.
3. Confirm via the block-documents API that `data.format_rule` is `null`.
4. Open the block in the UI editor (`/blocks/block/<id>/edit`). Click into the `format_rule` textarea (it renders empty, since `value ?? ""` displays `null` the same as no value) and save.
5. Re-check the block-documents API: `format_rule` key is now **absent** from `data` entirely (not `null`), and loading the block via the Python SDK now returns the class default (`"value.split(',')"`) instead of `None`.

(I have not separately confirmed whether saving the form *without* interacting with the `format_rule` field at all — only editing some other field — also reproduces this. Since the textarea's `onChange` only fires on user interaction, that path may or may not trigger the same key-deletion; the confirmed repro is interacting with the field itself.)

### Expected behavior

Either:
- The string input widget should be able to report an explicit `null` distinct from `undefined`, and the object-flush logic should preserve an explicitly-`null` value in the submitted document (not delete the key); or
- At minimum, the block-edit UI should not silently strip/alter fields the user never touched — only fields actually changed by the user should be able to affect the saved document.

### Additional context

This surfaced during real debugging of a healthcare-integration block (an HL7-code-extraction rule config) where the non-null default (`"value.split(',')"`) is only safe for one input shape, and `None` is required for a different, equally valid input shape (real HL7 field repetition, parsed into a list rather than a delimited string). A UI edit to an unrelated field on the same block silently reverted this to the default, breaking extraction for that site with no error — only a downstream symptom (fewer extracted values than expected).

This is likely related to (but distinct from) two older, closed issues about block-document editing that also stemmed from `merge_existing_data` semantics:
- #7264 — "Allow removal of field values for previously created block documents"
- #7516 — "Block attribute cannot be reverted to a default empty value from the UI" (fixed by introducing `merge_existing_data: false`, which appears to be the direct cause of *this* issue — full-replace-on-save means any field the widget layer can't correctly serialize as explicit `null` gets silently defaulted instead of preserved)

### Version info

```
Prefect: 3.6.24
```

issue_snapshot.title: V2 UI Custom Run crashes when an anyOf schema combines date and string enum
issue_snapshot.body:
## Bug summary

The V2 Custom Run page crashes with **`Invalid time value`** when an `anyOf` parameter contains both a date-formatted string and a string enum, and the deployment's value is an enum member.

The same deployment renders normally in the legacy V1 UI, which shows the `date` and `str` alternatives. The issue is isolated to the V2 form.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
from datetime import date
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel
from prefect import flow


class Builder(BaseModel):
    day: date | Literal[
        "today",
        "prev",
        "prev_td",
        "prev_td_if_not_td_today",
    ] = "prev_td"


@flow
def check(builder: Builder) -> None:
    pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    check.serve(
        name="ui-anyof-date-enum-repro",
        parameters={"builder": {"day": "prev_td"}},
    )
```

Open the deployment's **Custom Run** page in the V2 UI. The generated parameter schema is:

```json
{
  "anyOf": [
    { "format": "date", "type": "string" },
    {
      "enum": ["today", "prev", "prev_td", "prev_td_if_not_td_today"],
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Actual behavior

The V2 UI displays its error state:

> Something went wrong
>
> Invalid time value

It automatically retries but remains unusable.

### Expected behavior

The UI should select the enum branch for `"prev_td"`, render an enum control, and allow the flow run to be created.

### Source-level cause

[`getIndexForAnyOfPropertyValue`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/main/ui-v2/src/components/schemas/utilities/getIndexForAnyOfPropertyValue.ts#L47-L50) selects string alternatives using only `definition.type === "string"`. Both alternatives have that type, so it selects the first, date-formatted branch.

[`SchemaFormInputStringFormatDate`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/main/ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-string-format-date.tsx#L28-L31) then parses `"prev_td"` as a date; rendering formats that invalid date and throws `Invalid time value`.

A regression test should cover a string enum value with `anyOf: [{ type: "string", format: "date" }, { type: "string", enum: [...] }]` and assert that the enum branch is selected.

### Related work

[#20631](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/20631) fixed a different `anyOf` tab-selection issue involving typeless Prefect-kind values. The current `main` implementation still uses type-only matching for ordinary string values, so it does not cover this case.

## Version info

```text
Version:              3.8.1
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.14.6
Pydantic version:     2.13.4
Server type:          server
```

## Additional context

The failure was observed in the V2 UI error state. The same deployment opens successfully in the legacy V1 UI, which renders the `date` and `str` alternatives without a crash. Screenshots are available if needed.

issue_snapshot.title: Rewrite frame_buffer to use bytearray()
issue_snapshot.body:
Good artists copy, great artists steal. One of @njsmith's great decisions with [h11](https://github.com/njsmith/h11) was to write his [buffer](https://github.com/njsmith/h11/blob/master/h11/_receivebuffer.py) in terms of bytearray. This has some major efficiency gains on Python 3.4.

An easy win for us would be to rewrite the buffering internals of our frame buffer using h11's, while removing the things that h11's buffer implements that we don't need (in particular, any line-oriented constructs). Before we do it, we should write a benchmark of the buffering performance under reasonable HTTP/2 conditions to see what kind of improvements we see.

While I'm here: @fijal, the comments in h11's framebuffer say:

```python
# Note that starting in Python 3.4, deleting the initial n bytes from a
# bytearray is amortized O(n), thanks to some excellent work by Antoine
# Martin:
#
#     https://bugs.python.org/issue19087

...

# make sure PyPy also has the optimization
```

Does it?

issue_snapshot.title: Crash when using ListSerializer for an update on a model that has Unique together constraints
issue_snapshot.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have verified that that issue exists against the `master` branch of Django REST framework.
- [x] I have searched for similar issues in both open and closed tickets and cannot find a duplicate.
- [x] This is not a usage question. (Those should be directed to the [discussion group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/django-rest-framework) instead.)
- [x] This cannot be dealt with as a third party library. (We prefer new functionality to be [in the form of third party libraries](http://www.django-rest-framework.org/topics/third-party-resources/#about-third-party-packages) where possible.)
- [x] I have reduced the issue to the simplest possible case.
- [ ] I have included a failing test as a pull request. (If you are unable to do so we can still accept the issue.)


When using a [custom ListSerializer to update data](http://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/serializers/#customizing-multiple-update) and providing the instance as a queryset, if the model has some unique together constraint, the is_valid call crashes
## Steps to reproduce
Create a model with a unique together constraint
Create a serializer for this model
(Probably not needed) Create a custom list serializer with the `update` method overwritten and provide it to your model serializer with `list_serializer_class`
Now use the model serializer to serialize a list of data and provide both `many=True` and `instance=YourModel.objects.all()` to your serializer `__init__`
Call `serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)`

## Expected behavior
It should pass `is_valid` or at least not crash

## Actual behavior
It crashes in the [unique together validator](https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/master/rest_framework/validators.py#L154) because `instance` was not popped in the [many_init](https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/master/rest_framework/serializers.py#L145) so the child will receive a queryset instead of a model instance

## How to fix
Popping `instance` from the kwargs in [many_init](https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/master/rest_framework/serializers.py#L145) should do the trick but I'm not sure this won't introduce unforeseen problems
Moreover, the validators will probably fail because they will consider the call as a create rather than an update so here is that

issue_snapshot.title: Handle multiple Content-Length headers with the same value
issue_snapshot.body:
From RFC 7230 Section 3.3.2:

```
If a message is received that has multiple Content-Length header
   fields with field-values consisting of the same decimal value, or a
   single Content-Length header field with a field value containing a
   list of identical decimal values (e.g., "Content-Length: 42, 42"),
   indicating that duplicate Content-Length header fields have been
   generated or combined by an upstream message processor, then the
   recipient MUST either reject the message as invalid or replace the
   duplicated field-values with a single valid Content-Length field
   containing that decimal value prior to determining the message body
   length or forwarding the message.
```

Currently h11 will error out if multiple `Content-Length` headers are sent even when equal in value. Perhaps we should collapse the multiple headers into only one or allow the duplicate to pass through if the values are the same?

issue_snapshot.title: Increase/Decrease status code ranges
issue_snapshot.body:
Thank you for all the development. 

I have seen in h11/h11/_events.py / the handled status codes ranges are between `[200, 600)`. 

```
@dataclass(init=False, frozen=True)
class Response(_ResponseBase):
    """The beginning of an HTTP response.
    Fields:
    .. attribute:: status_code
       The status code of this response, as an integer. For an
       :class:`Response`, this is always in the range [200,
       600).
    .. attribute:: headers
       Request headers, represented as a list of (name, value) pairs. See
       :ref:`the header normalization rules <headers-format>` for details.
    .. attribute:: http_version
       The HTTP protocol version, represented as a byte string like
       ``b"1.1"``. See :ref:`the HTTP version normalization rules
       <http_version-format>` for details.
    .. attribute:: reason
       The reason phrase of this response, as a byte string. For example:
       ``b"OK"``, or ``b"Not Found"``.
    """

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not (200 <= self.status_code < 600):
            raise LocalProtocolError(
                "Response status_code should be in range [200, 600), not {}".format(
                    self.status_code
                )
            )
```

As this is the standard to follow, it's great to have it, but there are some http servers that don't follow the standard. What you think about adding the possibility to setup the status code ranges or increasing them for possible exceptional cases?
